candidates.original_title: Social attitudes and speech ratings: Effects of positive and negative bias on multiage listeners' judgments of second language speech
candidates.description: Social bias orientations (positive or negative) influence native listeners' ratings of non-native English speech across five linguistic dimensions (accentedness, comprehensibility, segmental errors, intonation, and flow)
candidates.citation_sentence: Reid et al. (2019) showed that 'native' listeners could be easily biased toward 'non-native' speech across five linguistic dimensions.

candidates.original_title: Social attitudes and speech ratings: Effects of positive and negative bias on multiage listeners' judgments of second language speech
candidates.description: Positive and negative social-bias orientations cause native English-speaking listeners to rate non-native English speech differently in terms of accentedness relative to a control condition.
candidates.citation_sentence: Reid et al. (2019) showed that "native" listeners could be easily biased toward "non-native" speech across five linguistic dimensions.
candidates.notes: One of five distinct speech-rating dimensions tested in the same replication experiment; the replication found no significant effect of bias manipulation. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
